rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 5 (score 53.64): wide 7-sensor array, kp 5.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.0, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12. Its progress was about 0.14 on the oval and s-bend and 0.10 on the slalom, and every trial still left the track at max_error of about 0.06. rms_error is about 0.03 and steering_oscillation is small, so the failure is a steady drift to the edge, not jitter. Score is mostly progress-driven at this stage (about 60 points at progress 0.14, rms 0.03, no line loss).

What I accept from the round-1 critique: (1) The draft stacked four untested changes (kd 0.8 to 1.2, wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10, mass 0.6 to 0.5, plus the array), so no race could attribute a result. I reject that stack. (2) The steady-drift evidence does not support kd as the remedy. Derivative action damps overshoot, and the data show none. (3) Narrowing wheel_track to 0.10 raises yaw gain by 1.2x, which is effectively a kp increase, and combining it with kd 1.2 shifts loop gain in two directions. I drop the track and mass changes.

What I changed: I start from the raced iteration-5 design, which is the only verified best, and change one variable. kp goes from 5.5 to 7.0 (about +27 percent). The steady drift at the edge suggests the robot is curvature-limited: the steering correction per metre of offset is too weak to hold the bends. Iteration 4 to 5 raised kp and progress rose, so this is the lever the data most directly support. kd stays at 0.4 so the loop does not get a second change. Geometry, weights, base_speed 1.0 and last_direction line loss are unchanged from the best race.

Rejected: the draft's kd 1.2 and track 0.10 stack, and any speed increase now. Raising speed before tracking holds would confound the test, and completion within 3 s needs about 1.5 m/s, which is out of reach until max_error drops below the limit.

Predictions (guesses, not expectations): progress on the s-bend and oval rises above 0.14, and max_error stays near or below 0.06. Decision rule for the next revision: if progress rises by at least 0.03 and steering_oscillation stays under about 0.2 with line_loss_events 0, continue raising kp in steps toward 9 before any speed change. If steering_oscillation grows sharply (above about 0.3) or progress falls, the loop is near its gain limit, so the next step is kd up (to about 0.8) with kp held at the last good value. If progress is unchanged at about 0.14, the drift is not curvature-limited, and the next test should target the start transient or the line-loss rule rather than gains.
